cap2_start: PHYS mid-152 CAPUT SECUNDUM / De S. Theologiae principiis…
titles: Sacred theology is a practical habit that teaches how to worship God and reach eternal life
Theology is called sacred over against profane science, and is a practical habit aiming at faith and eternal life
Third and fourth proofs from practical means and the mode of the primary object; theology is a practical habit
Four objections: theology holds theorems; the practical object is the doable; it treats theory as well as practice; eternal life is cognition
Replies to the first and second objections: Hebrew wise for just; theorems ordered to practice; the doable in itself or in another
Replies to the third and fourth objections; Gerhard on practical theology; orthodoxy and Christian life
Sacred theology is not among Aristotle's five logical virtues; spiritual things differ in kind from natural disciplines
Analogy with practical arts: fixed end, subject, and exact definition of the end as justification
From the defined end come the means, chiefly faith; theology differs from other disciplines in end, means, and subject
IV. Whether sacred theology is the same as the habit of faith and piety; science and wisdom
V–VI. Philosophical names of habits are alien if taken strictly; theology's principles are from revelation, method from industry
VII. The proper subject of sacred theology is the kingdom of God, and man as subject to God unto beatitude
VIII–IX. Theology does not swallow ethics and politics; metaphysics and ethics do not vanish but serve
X. The end of sacred theology: internal and external; the life of God; four grades of life; Cap. 1 close
